tanya: quick sync - we need to decide how much policy to push into the operator for dedicated pools. current tension: operator-local heuristics vs control-plane centralized policy.
oliver: operator-local is good for resilience during partition, but harder to reason about globally. control-plane gives single source of truth but needs low-latency API.
nora: For dedicated pools, network partitions are rare but possible. i propose hybrid: operator has a small, well-tested fallback policy for emergency eviction (simple: prefer best-effort, then lowest headroom), but day-to-day decisions come from control-plane `admit`/`evict_score` signals.
ops-miguel: How do we ensure operator fallback doesn't diverge and cause oscillation when control-plane recovers? we should include vector-clock like versioning in lease blob so operator can detect stale decisions.
tanya: Good point. plan: include `policy_version` and `policy_timestamp` in lease. operator ignores control-plane decision if timestamp older than operator's last-known policy apply time + drift window. fallback kicks in only when lease lacks recent policy or control-plane unreachable.
oliver: Also, operator should prioritize signals that it can measure locally: node health, GPU temp, container OOMs. control-plane can't see those quickly. fallback policy can include those local signals.
nora: right. fallback evacuation order: (1) tenants marked best-effort, (2) tenants with low credit balances, (3) oldest idle sessions, (4) tenants with no KV cache hits in last 10m. simple scoring.
ops-miguel: testing: inject network partition for 15m and verify no mass-evictions that violate tenant SLAs. record operator decisions in audit logs for later reconciliation.
anya: doc note: make sure SLA owners know fallback exists and may produce different eviction ordering for short partitions. add to runbook.
